title: Data Elements

blocks.text: A message is a single string, and the fields inside it are not separated by anything. Section 3.2 is the reason it can still be read: every data element has a declared format, and the format says how long it is.

A fixed-length element simply occupies its length. A variable-length one announces itself first — an LLVAR carries two digits of length before its value, an LLLVAR carries three. So a reader walks the message from left to right, and at each step it already knows how far to walk next. Get one length wrong and everything after it is garbage, which is why a malformed message usually fails somewhere other than where it is malformed.

Run `practice/fields/Fields.java` and read what it prints. Then change it: add a data element to the sample message and teach `unpack` to read it, or make it print the field numbers the bitmap claims are present.
Lesson: a practice with no grader

Nothing checks this file, and that is not a shortfall. Some material is worth running and reading rather than scoring, and a practice that says so honestly is better than one with a grader invented for it. There is a Run button here and no Submit button, because there is nothing to submit to.
